scope: synthesis questions for six books, returned in one pass
value: The first review output to produce new material rather than corrections. Per-entry review can only validate or reject what is already there; the gaps question is the only one that finds what is missing, and it is unanswerable without the scripture text alongside.

accepted.reason: Counter-example entry with empty practices — the drafter's own rule, broken a third time.
5:23-24 puts the initiative on the one who remembers his brother has something against him, regardless of fault.
Mary is asked twice and allowed to answer before anything is revealed — attention given before conclusion.
He washes the betrayer's feet and signals without naming. The enactment consists in what is withheld, which is weaker evidence than an act.

accepted_in_part.ref: Proverbs · Pride and the low place
accepted_in_part.reason: The verses plainly belong to the theme. PR25 does not: it is watching for the poor, the elderly and the stranger and giving up your own seat to them, while 25:6-7 is prudent self-placement — the other half of the same scene, and not the practice.

declined.reason: The verbs are keep, guard, put away, look straight ahead — nepsis rather than examination. Already tagged PR12, which is the practice the passage describes.

already_applied.note: The reviewer proposed +PR12; applied in the Jonah pass before this synthesis was requested.

reviewer_miss.question: stated claims
reviewer_miss.note: The prediction note was called fully validated. Half of it had already been retracted by the drafter: C11 quotes John 1:14 in its own text, so John was always going to close it, and that half was never a genuine forecast. The synthesis restated the prediction as confirmed without registering the retraction printed in the same note it was checking.
